rows.grounds: those to whom one becomes dear

items.question: What supreme attainments make a practitioner beloved by the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are attained together
Great accomplishment arises for the practitioner
Such attainment brings favor from the yoginis
items.inference: One who attains enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment becomes dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: One may attain enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment, and become dear to the yoginis.

items.question: Which chapter concludes after the teaching set in Candra-dvipa?
premises: The teaching context is Candra-dvipa
A section has emerged or concluded there
The section is identified by number
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes in the context of Candra-dvipa.
uncertainties: The exact sense of vinirgate as emerged or concluded is context-dependent
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvipa.

items.question: What bodily posture is visualized while surrounded by fire?
premises: The practitioner is surrounded by fire
The self is the object of contemplation
The posture involves standing on one foot
items.inference: One should visualize oneself surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize yourself surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

rows.grounds: thing requested to be made clear
past participle describing what is requested

items.question: What request is made to the deity regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity
The speaker seeks determination of knowledge
The speaker asks for it to be made manifest now
items.inference: The deity is asked to reveal the determination of knowledge to the speaker now.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me now.

items.question: What comprehensive division of eightfold groups is sought to be fully known?
premises: There is a division into groups of eight times eight
The speaker seeks full knowledge of this division
The knowledge is sought in an exhaustive manner
items.inference: The speaker seeks to fully know the division of the sixty-four groups.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean endlessly or in infinite detail
items.plain_english: I wish to fully know the division of the eight groups of eight, in all its extent.

items.question: How does the wheel in the secret place bring about swift accomplishment?
premises: There is a secret place
There is a wheel associated with it
This wheel accomplishes results quickly
items.inference: The wheel in the secret place is said to bring swift accomplishment.
uncertainties: The precise relation of yathā to the clause is slightly ambiguous
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel in the secret place is quickly accomplished.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the goddess for asking about a matter rare even for gods?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
The great goddess has asked a question
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess because her question concerns knowledge rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! You have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

rows.grounds: location or state of the syllable

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the brahmarandhra and the forehead?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
These are specific bodily placements
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is placed at the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is at the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the throat region and the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
These placements follow in sequence
items.inference: The syllable ṣa belongs to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the region of the throat, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows after the place-wheels have been declared?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Their meditation remains to be taught
The beloved is asked to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the first divine lotus visualized in relation to the first group of eight?
premises: The lotus is divine and eight-spoked
It is associated with the first group of eight
It is adorned by that group
items.inference: One should visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first group of eight.
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first group of eight.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned; sandhi form

items.question: What conduct must a practitioner abandon after gaining mental equanimity through practice?
premises: Practice leads to mental equanimity
Village customs represent ordinary social conduct
The practitioner is instructed to abandon them
items.inference: Through practice one becomes even-minded and should abandon village customs.
uncertainties: dharmañ shows sandhi before ca; taken as customs or duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the customs of village life.

items.question: What supernatural powers arise from this practice according to the teaching?
premises: Knowledge of hearing from afar is mentioned
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned
These are presented as attained powers
items.inference: The practice yields the power of distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting or paralyzing bonds or fetters
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly summarized for the goddess?
premises: Immortality is mentioned as an attainment
Transformation is mentioned as an attainment
The teaching is given in brief
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam could refer to transformation or reversal depending on context
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: The lotus is the second one
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is brightly illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What power of assuming multiple forms arises from one-pointed meditative focus?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
The practitioner gains a formative power
This power allows assuming many forms
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner may become angry
The power extends to the entire triple world
It includes both moving and unmoving beings
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: But when angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: The wheel is the third and great
It is associated with nine principles
It functions as a liberator
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: The exact set of nine tattvas is not specified in this verse
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this stage of practice?
premises: Wrinkles and grey hair are destroyed
Seeing from very far away is gained
These are presented as resulting powers
items.inference: This practice brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the power of seeing from afar.
items.plain_english: One gains the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the power to see from very far away.

items.question: What disciplined practice in solitude enables the creation of multiple forms?
premises: The practice is done in solitude
One should create many forms
One must be intent on meditation
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should practice creating many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result is assured for one devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice
Immortality is presented as an achievable result
The statement is emphatic
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death associated with aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is practiced
Death associated with age is the concern
The practice leads to overcoming it
items.inference: Through abstaining from food by day, one will overcome death due to aging.
uncertainties: The exact construction with gamiṣyate is idiomatic and context-dependent
items.plain_english: By not eating during the day, one will overcome death due to aging.

items.question: What youthful bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: The practice is constant yogic discipline
A specific age-form is mentioned
The practitioner attains that form
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What cosmic power arises from continually contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: One contemplates a smoke-colored form always
The triple world is the object affected
The practitioner gains the power to shake it
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
